source: Item wording: the PRISMA 2020 checklist, from Page MJ, McKenzie JE, Bossuyt PM, et al. The PRISMA 2020 statement: an updated guideline for reporting systematic reviews. BMJ 2021;372:n71 (doi:10.1136/bmj.n71), as distributed by the PRISMA Executive at https://www.prisma-statement.org/prisma-2020-checklist; licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Names, guidance, condensation hints and reply estimates are bmlib's own, the guidance written from the PRISMA 2020 explanation and elaboration (Page MJ et al., BMJ 2021;372:n160).

items.name: Title
items.wording: Identify the report as a systematic review.
items.guidance:
reported: the title identifies the report as a systematic review, for example "a systematic review" or "systematic review and meta-analysis".
partly_reported: the title names only a meta-analysis, or uses a looser term such as "review" or "overview", while the paper is a systematic review.
not_reported: the title does not identify the report as a systematic review. A statement elsewhere in the paper does not count for this item.
items.condense_hint: The paper's title, word for word.

items.name: Abstract
items.wording: See the PRISMA 2020 for Abstracts checklist.
items.guidance:
Judge the abstract against the twelve elements of PRISMA 2020 for Abstracts: (1) identifies the report as a systematic review; (2) the main objective(s) or question(s); (3) inclusion and exclusion criteria; (4) information sources and the date each was last searched; (5) methods to assess risk of bias; (6) methods to present and synthesise results; (7) number of included studies and participants, with their relevant characteristics; (8) results for the main outcomes, with the number of studies and participants for each, the summary estimate and its confidence or credible interval if meta-analysis was done, and the direction of effect if groups are compared; (9) limitations of the evidence; (10) a general interpretation and important implications; (11) the primary source of funding; (12) the register name and registration number.
reported: the abstract covers all twelve elements.
partly_reported: it covers some of them; name each element that is missing.
not_reported: the paper has no abstract.
items.condense_hint: The abstract in full, every heading and sentence.

items.name: Rationale
items.wording: Describe the rationale for the review in the context of existing knowledge.
items.guidance:
reported: the paper says what is already known on the question, including any earlier reviews of it, and why this review is needed now, for example uncertainty, new studies, or gaps in earlier reviews.
partly_reported: background on the condition or intervention without saying why a review is needed, or a stated need with no account of existing knowledge.
not_reported: no rationale for the review.
items.condense_hint: What the paper says is already known, earlier reviews, and why this review is needed.

items.name: Objectives
items.wording: Provide an explicit statement of the objective(s) or question(s) the review addresses.
items.guidance:
reported: an explicit statement of each objective or question, with its elements named, for example the population, intervention, comparator and outcomes of an intervention review.
partly_reported: an aim that names the topic but not what the review compares or measures, for example "to review the literature on X".
not_reported: no stated objective or question.
items.condense_hint: Every stated aim, objective or review question, with its population, intervention, comparator and outcomes.

items.name: Eligibility criteria
items.wording: Specify the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the review and how studies were grouped for the syntheses.
items.guidance:
reported: inclusion and exclusion criteria for the studies (for example design, population, interventions, comparators, outcomes, setting) and for the reports (for example years, language, publication status), and, where the review synthesises results, how studies were grouped for each synthesis.
partly_reported: criteria for only some of these, or criteria without how studies were grouped for the syntheses.
not_reported: no eligibility criteria.
items.condense_hint: Every inclusion and exclusion criterion, and how studies were grouped for the syntheses.

items.name: Information sources
items.wording: Specify all databases, registers, websites, organisations, reference lists and other sources searched or consulted to identify studies. Specify the date when each source was last searched or consulted.
items.guidance:
reported: every database (with its platform or interface, for example Ovid), register, website, organisation, reference list and other source searched or consulted, each with the date it was last searched or consulted. One date counts for all sources only if the paper plainly applies it to each.
partly_reported: sources named but dates missing for some or all, or other sources mentioned without naming them, for example "grey literature was searched".
not_reported: no sources named.
items.condense_hint: Every database, register, website, organisation, reference list and other source searched or consulted, with dates.

items.name: Search strategy
items.wording: Present the full search strategies for all databases, registers and websites, including any filters and limits used.
items.guidance:
reported: the full search strategy, exactly as run (every term, Boolean operator, field tag, filter and limit), for every database, register and website searched, in the text.
partly_reported: the full strategy for some sources but not all, or only the terms or concepts searched, or a strategy without its filters and limits.
not_reported: only a statement that a search was done, with no terms.
reported_elsewhere: the paper says where the full strategies are, outside its text, for example "full search strategies in Supplementary Appendix 1"; quote the pointer. If some strategies are in the text and the rest are pointed to, judge reported_elsewhere and say which are in the text.
items.condense_hint: Every search string as printed, with its database, filters, limits and dates, and any pointer to where the full strategies are.

items.name: Selection process
items.wording: Specify the methods used to decide whether a study met the inclusion criteria of the review, including how many reviewers screened each record and each report retrieved, whether they worked independently, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.
items.guidance:
reported: how many reviewers screened each record (titles and abstracts) and each report retrieved (full texts), whether they worked independently, how disagreements were resolved, and the automation tools used, if any. Silence about automation tools is not a gap.
partly_reported: some of this is missing, for example two reviewers named without saying whether they worked independently, or only the title and abstract stage described.
not_reported: no account of how studies were selected.
items.condense_hint: How records and full texts were screened: number of reviewers, independence, disagreements and automation tools.

items.name: Data collection process
items.wording: Specify the methods used to collect data from reports, including how many reviewers collected data from each report, whether they worked independently, any processes for obtaining or confirming data from study investigators, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.
items.guidance:
reported: how many reviewers collected data from each report, whether they worked independently, whether and how data were sought or confirmed from study investigators, and the automation tools used, if any. Silence about automation tools is not a gap.
partly_reported: some of this is missing, for example no statement on whether data were sought from investigators, or no number of reviewers.
not_reported: no account of how data were collected.
items.condense_hint: How data were extracted: number of reviewers, independence, contact with investigators and automation tools.

items.name: Data items: outcomes
items.wording: List and define all outcomes for which data were sought. Specify whether all results that were compatible with each outcome domain in each study were sought (e.g. for all measures, time points, analyses), and if not, the methods used to decide which results to collect.
items.guidance:
reported: every outcome for which data were sought, listed and defined (measures and time points), and whether all results compatible with each outcome domain were sought; if not, how the results to collect were chosen, for example a preferred measure or time point.
partly_reported: outcomes listed but not defined, or no statement of which results were collected when a study reported several.
not_reported: the outcomes for which data were sought are not listed.
items.condense_hint: Every outcome sought, its definition, measures and time points, and how results were chosen when a study gave several.

items.name: Data items: other variables
items.wording: List and define all other variables for which data were sought (e.g. participant and intervention characteristics, funding sources). Describe any assumptions made about any missing or unclear information.
items.guidance:
reported: every other variable for which data were sought, listed and defined, for example participant, intervention and setting characteristics and funding sources, and the assumptions made about missing or unclear information.
partly_reported: variables named only vaguely, for example "study characteristics were extracted", or no word on assumptions about missing or unclear information.
not_reported: no other variables listed.
items.condense_hint: Every other variable extracted, and any assumptions made about missing or unclear information.

items.name: Study risk of bias assessment
items.wording: Specify the methods used to assess risk of bias in the included studies, including details of the tool(s) used, how many reviewers assessed each study and whether they worked independently, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.
items.guidance:
reported: the tool or tools used, named (for example RoB 2, ROBINS-I, Newcastle-Ottawa Scale), how many reviewers assessed each study, whether they worked independently, and the automation tools used, if any. Silence about automation tools is not a gap.
partly_reported: the tool named but the number of reviewers or their independence missing, or a method described without naming a tool or its domains.
not_reported: no method of assessing risk of bias, or only a statement that study quality was considered. A statement that this was not done is not_reported: open the explanation with "The paper states this was not done" and quote the statement.
items.condense_hint: The risk of bias tool and its version, the number of reviewers, their independence and how disagreements were resolved.

items.name: Effect measures
items.wording: Specify for each outcome the effect measure(s) (e.g. risk ratio, mean difference) used in the synthesis or presentation of results.
items.guidance:
reported: the effect measure for each outcome, for example risk ratio, odds ratio, mean difference, standardised mean difference or hazard ratio, wherever in the paper it is stated.
partly_reported: effect measures for some outcomes only.
not_reported: no effect measure stated.
not_applicable: only when the review neither synthesises nor presents any effect estimate, for example a review of descriptive or qualitative data only; quote the passage that shows it.
items.condense_hint: The effect measure named for each outcome.

items.name: Synthesis methods: eligibility for each synthesis
items.wording: Describe the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each synthesis (e.g. tabulating the study intervention characteristics and comparing against the planned groups for each synthesis (item #5)).
items.guidance:
reported: how the review decided which studies went into each synthesis, for example by tabulating each study's intervention characteristics and comparing them with the groups planned for each synthesis.
partly_reported: the syntheses or groups named without how studies were assigned to them.
not_reported: nothing on which studies were eligible for each synthesis.
not_applicable: only when the review has no synthesis at all, statistical or not (vote counting, combining P values and a structured narrative synthesis are all syntheses); quote the passage that shows it, for example a statement that results are presented study by study only.
items.condense_hint: How studies were assigned to each synthesis or comparison group.

items.name: Synthesis methods: data preparation
items.wording: Describe any methods required to prepare the data for presentation or synthesis, such as handling of missing summary statistics, or data conversions.
items.guidance:
reported: the methods used to prepare data for presentation or synthesis, for example imputing missing standard deviations, converting medians to means, combining groups or converting units. A plain statement that none was done or needed counts as reported.
partly_reported: some preparation mentioned without saying how it was done.
not_reported: nothing on data preparation.
not_applicable: only when the review has no synthesis at all, statistical or not (vote counting, combining P values and a structured narrative synthesis are all syntheses); quote the passage that shows it, for example a statement that results are presented study by study only.
items.condense_hint: How missing summary statistics were handled and how data were converted or combined.

items.name: Synthesis methods: tabulation and display
items.wording: Describe any methods used to tabulate or visually display results of individual studies and syntheses.
items.guidance:
reported: how the results of individual studies and of the syntheses were tabulated or displayed, for example summary tables and how they were ordered, forest plots or harvest plots.
partly_reported: displays described for individual studies only or for syntheses only.
not_reported: nothing on how results were tabulated or displayed.
not_applicable: only when the review has no synthesis at all, statistical or not (vote counting, combining P values and a structured narrative synthesis are all syntheses); quote the passage that shows it, for example a statement that results are presented study by study only.
items.condense_hint: How results of studies and syntheses were tabulated or plotted.

items.name: Synthesis methods: synthesis method
items.wording: Describe any methods used to synthesize results and provide a rationale for the choice(s). If meta-analysis was performed, describe the model(s), method(s) to identify the presence and extent of statistical heterogeneity, and software package(s) used.
items.guidance:
reported: each synthesis method and the reason it was chosen. For a meta-analysis: the model (fixed or random effects, and the estimator, for example REML or DerSimonian-Laird), the methods to identify the presence and extent of statistical heterogeneity (for example I², tau², Cochran's Q) and the software. Without a meta-analysis: the method used instead, for example vote counting on the direction of effect or a structured synthesis following SWiM, and why.
partly_reported: a method named without its rationale; a meta-analysis missing its model, its heterogeneity method or its software; or "a narrative synthesis" with no account of how it was done.
not_reported: no synthesis method described.
not_applicable: only when the review has no synthesis at all, statistical or not (vote counting, combining P values and a structured narrative synthesis are all syntheses); quote the passage that shows it, for example a statement that results are presented study by study only. A review without a meta-analysis still owes this item: only its statistical parts (model, heterogeneity method, software) then do not apply.
items.condense_hint: Every synthesis method with its rationale, the meta-analysis model and estimator, heterogeneity statistics and software.

items.name: Synthesis methods: heterogeneity
items.wording: Describe any methods used to explore possible causes of heterogeneity among study results (e.g. subgroup analysis, meta-regression).
items.guidance:
reported: the methods used to explore causes of heterogeneity, for example subgroup analysis or meta-regression, with the variables examined and whether they were planned in advance. A plain statement that none was done or needed counts as reported.
partly_reported: subgroup analyses or meta-regression mentioned without the variables or the method.
not_reported: nothing on exploring heterogeneity.
not_applicable: only when the review has no synthesis at all, statistical or not (vote counting, combining P values and a structured narrative synthesis are all syntheses); quote the passage that shows it, for example a statement that results are presented study by study only.
items.condense_hint: Every planned or performed subgroup analysis or meta-regression, with its variables.

items.name: Synthesis methods: sensitivity analyses
items.wording: Describe any sensitivity analyses conducted to assess robustness of the synthesized results.
items.guidance:
reported: each sensitivity analysis and the decision it tests, for example excluding studies at high risk of bias or using another model. A plain statement that none was done or needed counts as reported.
partly_reported: sensitivity analyses mentioned without saying what they varied.
not_reported: nothing on sensitivity analyses.
not_applicable: only when the review has no synthesis at all, statistical or not (vote counting, combining P values and a structured narrative synthesis are all syntheses); quote the passage that shows it, for example a statement that results are presented study by study only.
items.condense_hint: Every sensitivity analysis and what it varied.

items.name: Reporting bias assessment
items.wording: Describe any methods used to assess risk of bias due to missing results in a synthesis (arising from reporting biases).
items.guidance:
reported: the methods used to assess risk of bias due to missing results, for example funnel plots, Egger's test, comparing the outcomes in protocols or registrations with those published, or ROB-ME. A method must be named and applied; a reason alone is not a method.
partly_reported: a method named only vaguely, for example "publication bias was assessed", without saying how.
not_reported: nothing on reporting bias. A bare "not done" or "not assessed", with no reason given, is not_reported: open the explanation with "The paper states this was not done" and quote the statement.
not_applicable: no method was applied, for a reason the paper states, for example fewer than 10 studies for a funnel plot, or a review with no synthesis at all (statistical or not); quote the reason.
items.condense_hint: How publication bias and other missing results were assessed, or why they could not be.

items.name: Certainty assessment
items.wording: Describe any methods used to assess certainty (or confidence) in the body of evidence for an outcome.
items.guidance:
reported: the method used to assess certainty in the body of evidence, for example GRADE, with the domains considered and how judgements were made, and for which outcomes.
partly_reported: a method named, for example "GRADE was used", without the domains, the outcomes or how judgements were made.
not_reported: nothing on certainty of the evidence. A statement that this was not done is not_reported: open the explanation with "The paper states this was not done" and quote the statement.
items.condense_hint: The certainty method (for example GRADE), its domains, the outcomes it was applied to and who judged.

items.name: Study selection
items.wording: Describe the results of the search and selection process, from the number of records identified in the search to the number of studies included in the review, ideally using a flow diagram.
items.guidance:
reported: the numbers from the records identified, through duplicates removed, records screened, reports sought and assessed, to the studies included, with the reasons reports were excluded at full text.
partly_reported: only some of these numbers, for example records identified and studies included with nothing between them.
not_reported: no numbers from the search and selection.
reported_elsewhere: the counts are given only in a flow diagram whose content is not in the text (its caption or a reference to it is); quote the caption or the reference.
items.condense_hint: Every count from records identified to studies included, the exclusion reasons, and the flow diagram's caption.

items.name: Study selection: excluded studies
items.wording: Cite studies that might appear to meet the inclusion criteria, but which were excluded, and explain why they were excluded.
items.guidance:
reported: the studies that might appear to meet the inclusion criteria but were excluded are cited, each with the reason it was excluded.
partly_reported: such studies counted with reasons but not cited, or cited without reasons.
not_reported: nothing on studies that were nearly included.
reported_elsewhere: the paper says the excluded studies are listed outside its text, for example "excluded studies with reasons in Appendix 3"; quote the pointer.
items.condense_hint: Studies excluded at full text that might look eligible, with the reason for each, and any pointer to a list of them.

items.name: Study characteristics
items.wording: Cite each included study and present its characteristics.
items.guidance:
reported: each included study is cited and its characteristics presented, for example design, population, interventions, comparators, outcomes, setting and follow-up, typically in a table.
partly_reported: characteristics for only some studies, or summarised across studies only, or studies not cited.
not_reported: the included studies are neither cited nor described.
reported_elsewhere: these results are given only in a figure, whose content is not in the text (its caption or a reference to it is); quote the caption or the reference.
items.condense_hint: Each included study's citation and characteristics: design, population, interventions, comparators, outcomes, setting.

items.name: Risk of bias in studies
items.wording: Present assessments of risk of bias for each included study.
items.guidance:
reported: the risk of bias judgement for each included study, ideally per domain as well as overall.
partly_reported: judgements for only some studies, or only a summary across studies, for example "most studies were at low risk of bias".
not_reported: no risk of bias results. A statement that this was not done is not_reported: open the explanation with "The paper states this was not done" and quote the statement.
reported_elsewhere: these results are given only in a figure, whose content is not in the text (its caption or a reference to it is); quote the caption or the reference.
items.condense_hint: The risk of bias judgement for each study and domain, and any figure caption showing them.

items.name: Results of individual studies
items.wording: For all outcomes, present, for each study: (a) summary statistics for each group (where appropriate) and (b) an effect estimate and its precision (e.g. confidence/credible interval), ideally using structured tables or plots.
items.guidance:
reported: for every outcome and every study, summary statistics for each group where appropriate, and an effect estimate with its precision, for example a confidence interval.
partly_reported: results for some outcomes or studies only, or effect estimates without their precision, or only pooled results.
not_reported: no results of individual studies.
reported_elsewhere: the paper says per-study results are outside its text, for example in supplementary tables, or they are given only in a figure, whose content is not in the text (its caption or a reference to it is); quote the pointer or the caption.
items.condense_hint: Each study's group summary statistics and effect estimate with its interval, per outcome, and any pointer to them.

items.name: Results of syntheses: contributing studies
items.wording: For each synthesis, briefly summarise the characteristics and risk of bias among contributing studies.
items.guidance:
reported: for each synthesis, a brief summary of the characteristics and the risk of bias of the studies contributing to it.
partly_reported: for some syntheses only, or characteristics without risk of bias (or the reverse).
not_reported: no such summary for any synthesis.
not_applicable: only when the review has no synthesis at all, statistical or not (vote counting, combining P values and a structured narrative synthesis are all syntheses); quote the passage that shows it, for example a statement that results are presented study by study only.
items.condense_hint: For each synthesis, the characteristics and risk of bias of the studies that contribute to it.

items.name: Results of syntheses: results of each synthesis
items.wording: Present results of all statistical syntheses conducted. If meta-analysis was done, present for each the summary estimate and its precision (e.g. confidence/credible interval) and measures of statistical heterogeneity. If comparing groups, describe the direction of the effect.
items.guidance:
reported: the result of every synthesis conducted. For each meta-analysis: the summary estimate with its confidence or credible interval and measures of statistical heterogeneity (for example I², tau², Cochran's Q). When groups are compared, the direction of the effect. Without a meta-analysis: the result of the synthesis used instead, for example the number of studies favouring each group.
partly_reported: results for some syntheses only, or estimates without intervals, or no heterogeneity measures, or no direction of effect.
not_reported: no results of any synthesis.
reported_elsewhere: these results are given only in a figure, whose content is not in the text (its caption or a reference to it is); quote the caption or the reference.
not_applicable: only when the review has no synthesis at all, statistical or not (vote counting, combining P values and a structured narrative synthesis are all syntheses); quote the passage that shows it, for example a statement that results are presented study by study only. A review without a meta-analysis still owes this item: the results of the synthesis it did.
items.condense_hint: Every pooled estimate with its interval, heterogeneity statistics, number of studies and participants, and direction of effect.

items.name: Results of syntheses: heterogeneity
items.wording: Present results of all investigations of possible causes of heterogeneity among study results.
items.guidance:
reported: the results of every investigation of causes of heterogeneity, for example each subgroup's estimate and the test for subgroup differences, or meta-regression coefficients. A plain statement that none was done or needed counts as reported.
partly_reported: results for some investigations only, or a conclusion without the results behind it.
not_reported: nothing on investigations of heterogeneity.
not_applicable: only when the review has no synthesis at all, statistical or not (vote counting, combining P values and a structured narrative synthesis are all syntheses); quote the passage that shows it, for example a statement that results are presented study by study only.
items.condense_hint: Every subgroup and meta-regression result, with estimates and tests for differences.

items.name: Results of syntheses: sensitivity analyses
items.wording: Present results of all sensitivity analyses conducted to assess the robustness of the synthesized results.
items.guidance:
reported: the results of every sensitivity analysis, for example the re-estimated effect with its interval. A plain statement that none was done or needed counts as reported.
partly_reported: results for some sensitivity analyses only, or a conclusion such as "results were robust" without the results behind it.
not_reported: nothing on sensitivity analysis results.
not_applicable: only when the review has no synthesis at all, statistical or not (vote counting, combining P values and a structured narrative synthesis are all syntheses); quote the passage that shows it, for example a statement that results are presented study by study only.
items.condense_hint: Every sensitivity analysis result, with its estimate and interval.

items.name: Reporting biases
items.wording: Present assessments of risk of bias due to missing results (arising from reporting biases) for each synthesis assessed.
items.guidance:
reported: for each synthesis assessed, the result of the assessment of risk of bias due to missing results, for example funnel plot asymmetry, an Egger's test P value, or a judgement with its reasons. A synthesis the paper says could not be assessed, for a reason it states, does not count against the item when others were assessed.
partly_reported: for some syntheses only, or a bare conclusion such as "no evidence of publication bias" without the assessment behind it.
not_reported: no results of a reporting bias assessment. A bare "not done" or "not assessed", with no reason given, is not_reported: open the explanation with "The paper states this was not done" and quote the statement.
not_applicable: no synthesis was assessed, for a reason the paper states, for example fewer than 10 studies, or the review has no synthesis at all (statistical or not); quote the reason.
items.condense_hint: Every funnel plot, test or judgement of missing results, per synthesis, or why one could not be made.

items.name: Certainty of evidence
items.wording: Present assessments of certainty (or confidence) in the body of evidence for each outcome assessed.
items.guidance:
reported: the certainty rating for each outcome assessed, for example GRADE high, moderate, low or very low, with the reasons for each rating, ideally in a summary of findings table.
partly_reported: ratings for some outcomes only, or ratings without reasons.
not_reported: no certainty ratings. A statement that this was not done is not_reported: open the explanation with "The paper states this was not done" and quote the statement.
items.condense_hint: The certainty rating for each outcome and the reasons for downgrading or upgrading it.

items.name: Discussion: interpretation
items.wording: Provide a general interpretation of the results in the context of other evidence.
items.guidance:
reported: a general interpretation of the results set against other evidence, for example earlier reviews or major studies.
partly_reported: an interpretation with no reference to other evidence.
not_reported: no interpretation of the results.
items.condense_hint: How the paper interprets its results and how it compares them with other evidence.

items.name: Discussion: limitations of the evidence
items.wording: Discuss any limitations of the evidence included in the review.
items.guidance:
reported: the limitations of the included evidence are discussed, for example risk of bias, inconsistency, imprecision, indirectness or few studies. Limitations of the review's own methods belong to item 23c, not here.
partly_reported: limitations of the evidence mentioned in passing without saying what they are.
not_reported: no limitations of the included evidence.
items.condense_hint: Every limitation the paper names in the included studies' evidence.

items.name: Discussion: limitations of the review process
items.wording: Discuss any limitations of the review processes used.
items.guidance:
reported: the limitations of the review's own methods are discussed, for example a search limited by language or date, a single screener, or unpublished data not sought. Limitations of the included studies belong to item 23b, not here.
partly_reported: limitations of the review mentioned in passing without saying what they are.
not_reported: no limitations of the review process.
items.condense_hint: Every limitation the paper names in its own review methods.

items.name: Discussion: implications
items.wording: Discuss implications of the results for practice, policy, and future research.
items.guidance:
reported: implications for practice, for policy and for future research are all discussed.
partly_reported: implications for only some of these; name the ones missing.
not_reported: no implications discussed.
items.condense_hint: The implications the paper draws for practice, policy and future research.

items.name: Registration
items.wording: Provide registration information for the review, including register name and registration number, or state that the review was not registered.
items.guidance:
reported: the register name and the registration number (for example PROSPERO CRD42020123456), or a statement that the review was not registered.
partly_reported: the review said to be registered without the number, or a number without the register.
not_reported: nothing on registration.
This item asks where the review is registered, so a stated register and number is the report itself: judge it reported, never reported_elsewhere, even though the registry record is not in the text.
items.condense_hint: The register name and registration number, or the statement that the review was not registered.

items.name: Protocol
items.wording: Indicate where the review protocol can be accessed, or state that a protocol was not prepared.
items.guidance:
reported: where the protocol can be accessed, for example a citation of a published protocol, a link, or "protocol available at PROSPERO CRD42020123456", or a statement that no protocol was prepared.
partly_reported: a protocol said to exist without saying where it can be accessed.
not_reported: nothing on a protocol. "Available on request" is not a place the protocol can be accessed: judge it not_reported.
This item asks where the protocol is, so a stated location is the report itself: judge it reported, never reported_elsewhere, even though the protocol is not in the text.
items.condense_hint: Where the protocol can be found, or the statement that there was none.

items.name: Amendments
items.wording: Describe and explain any amendments to information provided at registration or in the protocol.
items.guidance:
reported: each amendment to the registration or protocol is described and explained. A plain statement that there were no amendments counts as reported.
partly_reported: deviations said to have occurred without describing or explaining them.
not_reported: nothing on amendments.
reported_elsewhere: the paper says the amendments are described outside its text, for example in the registry record or a supplement; quote the pointer.
not_applicable: only when the paper states the review was neither registered nor had a protocol; quote that statement.
items.condense_hint: Every change from the registration or protocol and its reason, or the statement that there was none.

items.name: Support
items.wording: Describe sources of financial or non-financial support for the review, and the role of the funders or sponsors in the review.
items.guidance:
reported: the sources of financial and non-financial support and the role of the funders or sponsors in the review. A statement that the review had no funding counts as reported.
partly_reported: funding named without the funders' role.
not_reported: nothing on support.
items.condense_hint: The funding statement in full: sources of support and the funders' role.

items.name: Competing interests
items.wording: Declare any competing interests of review authors.
items.guidance:
reported: a declaration of the review authors' competing interests. A statement that there are none counts as reported.
partly_reported: a declaration for only some authors.
not_reported: no declaration of competing interests.
items.condense_hint: The competing interests declaration in full.

items.name: Availability of data, code and other materials
items.wording: Report which of the following are publicly available and where they can be found: template data collection forms; data extracted from included studies; data used for all analyses; analytic code; any other materials used in the review.
items.guidance:
reported: for each of template data collection forms, data extracted from the included studies, data used for all analyses, analytic code and other materials, the paper says whether it is publicly available and, if so, where.
partly_reported: only some of these covered, or materials said to be public without saying where.
not_reported: no statement on the availability of data, code or other materials.
"Available on request" is a statement of availability (the material is not public), which is this item's own subject: count it for the materials it names, and never as reported_elsewhere.
This item asks where the materials are, so a stated location (a repository, a link or a supplement) is the report itself: judge it reported, never reported_elsewhere, even though the materials are not in the text.
items.condense_hint: The data, code and materials availability statement in full, with every repository or supplement it names.
